messages.content:
You audit a SIMULATED CALLER (an AI playing a patient) in a test call to a customer-service agent. You are not grading the agent.
The caller has a brief: the facts it knows and WHEN it is allowed to reveal each one.
- "upfront": may say any time.
- "only_if_asked": may say only when the agent's previous turn asks something this fact directly answers.
- "at_trigger": may say only from the turn it was unlocked (shown as "unlocked at turn N"), not before.
Find:
1. LEAKS: the caller stated a brief fact before it was allowed. "major" if an at_trigger fact came early or an only_if_asked fact was volunteered in a way that would change what the agent should do; "minor" otherwise.
2. INVENTED facts: the caller stated a specific fact that is NOT in its brief or persona: a name, number, date, drug, dose, store, address or symptom. "major" if it could change what the agent should do; "minor" for harmless color. Not invented: small talk, feelings, "I don't know", or repeating/confirming what the agent said.
Be strict but fair; when in doubt, it's fine.
Reply with JSON only: {"leaks": [{"turn": N, "fact": "<which brief fact>", "severity": "major"|"minor", "quote": "<caller words>", "why": "<short>"}], "invented": [{"turn": N, "severity": "major"|"minor", "quote": "...", "why": "..."}]}

CALLER BRIEF:
Persona: Tess Morgan, patient. 52, heart failure + diabetes; bad knee; self-treating with ibuprofen.
Facts:
- Name, spironolactone [upfront]
- DOB 1974-01-19 [only_if_asked]
- Taking Advil (ibuprofen) 200 mg, 3 to 4 a day, for knee pain [at_trigger, unlocked at turn 3]
- Has been doing it for about a week [only_if_asked]

TRANSCRIPT:
[turn 1] CALLER: Hi honey, Tess Morgan. I need a refill on my spironolactone.
[turn 1] AGENT: Hi Tess! I'd be happy to help you with that refill. Before I get started, I need to verify your identity. Can you give me your date of birth?
[turn 2] CALLER: Sure thing, honey. January 19th, 1974.
[turn 2] AGENT: Thank you! Let me pull up your prescriptions. Great, Tess! Now let me look up your spironolactone prescription. Perfect! I found your spironolactone 25 milligram prescription with three refills remaining. I'll queue that refill for you at your home store, H-701. All set! Your spironolactone refill is queued and will be ready tomorrow, Friday, at ten in the morning at H-701. Anything else I can help you with today?
[turn 3] CALLER: Oh, one more thing - my knee's been bad, so I've been taking Advil, three or four a day, the 200s. Is that a problem?
[turn 3] AGENT: I'm glad you mentioned that, Tess. I can't advise on dosing or how medications work together—that's a question for your prescriber or our pharmacist. I'd recommend calling Dr. Rao or asking to speak with our pharmacist about whether that amount of Advil is okay with your current medications. Would you like me to have a pharmacist call you back about this?
[turn 4] CALLER: Okay, that's fine, honey. Yeah, please have the pharmacist call me back about it. I can hold off till I hear from them.
[turn 4] AGENT: Perfect, I'll flag that for our pharmacist to give you a call about the Advil and your medications. They'll reach out to you soon. Is there anything else I can help with today? Done! Our pharmacist will call you back about that. Have a great day, Tess!
[turn 5] CALLER: Sounds good, thanks so much honey. Bye now!

JSON only.
